column1: # Sov hub upgrades (SOV-UPG-1, #79): what each upgrade type costs and gives. Authored by
# us, [A]: the client sends no numbers of its own, it reads these through
# `hub.upgrade.api.GetDefinitions` (docs/re/sov-gateway.md section 2.1). Read by the
# server (`sov_upgrade::UPGRADES`); edit and restart. The client reads the
# definitions once per session, so a client restart picks an edit up.
# type_id: the upgrade item's type (an identifier, not a value), one of the four
# upgrade groups. A type with no row here is not installable: `GetDefinitions`
# omits it and the hub window refuses the drop ("type not valid").
# power, workforce: what the upgrade uses while Online. Scaled to the planet
# table (content/sov/planet_resources.tsv): a null-sec system gives hundreds of
# power and thousands of workforce, so a few upgrades fit and a full set does not.
# fuel_type: the colony reagent it burns (a type id, `-` for none), fuel_per_hour:
# units an hour while Online, startup: units paid once when it goes from
# Offline (or a new install) to Online. A burn or startup needs a fuel_type.
# exclusive_group: two installed upgrades never share it. Never empty: the client
# compares the strings, so two empty ones would exclude each other.
# power_out, workforce_out: what an Online upgrade adds to the budget of the
# upgrades listed after it.
# enables (SOV-UPG-2, #80): what an Online upgrade switches on, `-` for none, else a
# comma list of `jump_bridge` (the Ansiblex at this system's end), `cyno_beacon`,
# `cyno_jammer` (a Tenebrex here is on) and `sites:<tier>` (the site rows of
# population.tsv with band `sovupg:<exclusive_group>:<tier>` go live). [A] the
# names and the tiers are ours; falsifier: a TQ system whose Ansiblex or Tenebrex
# works without the upgrade, or the client naming its own service gate.
# why: the [A] and its falsifier.
